text:
incident-bot: Pager — P1: hydra-enterprise (private VPC) auth failures detected for dedicated pool hydra-dpool-2. Multiple auth proxy TLS handshakes failing (client auth).
laura_ops: hitting this now, seeing ~40% of requests to /v1/auth/introspect returning 503 from our identity-proxy. Customer reported increased 401 spikes.
dan_oncall: I'm on call — joining. @laura_ops can you post a short impact summary and a sample error log?
laura_ops: impact: Hydra (enterprise) users in eu-central can’t create new sessions; existing sessions intermittently fail token validation. Backend queue backs up, tail latency spiking.
laura_ops: sample from identity-proxy logs:
```
2026-03-15T09:12:34Z ERROR tls: handshake failure: remote error: tls: bad certificate (verify return code: 20)
2026-03-15T09:12:34Z WARN  sni: expected tenant SNI "hydra.tenant-12.vpc.redwood", got "hydra.edge.redwood"; closing
```
eng-alex: that SNI line stands out — LB recently rolled edge cert/hostname rewrite yesterday in eu-central-1. Sounds like SNI mapping changed and the identity-proxy enforces tenant-specific SNI for mTLS.
eng-sam: cross-checking envoy config on auth-bridge: our SNI routing table has explicit entries per tenant. If the LB overrides SNI, the client cert path will be rejected.
sre-jordan: paging infra/edge oncall. @deploy-bot can you confirm if the TLS termination change was rolled to eu-central?
deploy-bot: Deployment record: edge-rewrite:v3.4.1 deployed 2026-03-15T03:07:00Z to eu-central-1. No rollbacks recorded.
laura_ops: reached out to customer sec contact. @sec-irene any changes on your side?
sec-irene: we did a certificate bundle rotation last night but we did not change SNI. We see the same handshake rejects from our side for outbound client connections to your auth endpoint.
dan_oncall: OK — immediate mitigation options: 1) route Hydra traffic to the auth-bridge-fallback fleet that does not enforce per-tenant SNI OR 2) temporarily relax strict SNI enforcement on identity-proxy for hydra tenant. Which is least risk?
eng-alex: fallback fleet is warmed and can take traffic; it lacks the strict tenant isolation but preserves auth semantics for now. Option 1 buys time while infra corrects the SNI rewrite.
laura_ops: I'll open a temp route and move 25% traffic, monitor. Rolling now.
laura_ops: `kubectl apply -f route-hydra-fallback-25.yaml`
laura_ops: Routing change applied. Monitoring logs.
laura_ops: error rate drops to ~12% after routing 25%. Latency down a notch.
laura_ops: increasing to 60% gradually.
eng-sam: while traffic moves, let's confirm root cause: capture TLS ClientHello from failing connection to see SNI value. @sre-jordan can you run tcpdump on auth-proxy pod and extract first 1kB?
sre-jordan: tcpdump capture posted to private infra bucket /captures/hydra-2765432109.pcap.gz (link sent in PM). Quick grep: most ClientHello SNI fields are `hydra.edge.redwood` instead of tenant SNI.
eng-alex: that matches LB rewrite. Need infra to revert SNI rewrite or update their mapping so downstream sees tenant SNI.
sre-jordan: infra oncall (edge-team) acknowledged — they will rollback rewrite in eu-central now. ETA ~7 minutes.
sec-irene: thanks, we prefer strict SNI but appreciate the fallback. Customer accepts brief reduced isolation while fix is applied.
laura_ops: current status: 60% traffic on fallback, error rate ~3%, request backlog shrinking. Customer notified.
dan_oncall: handing off primary incident lead to @eng-alex for post-fix verification and root-cause. I'll stay until rollback completes.
eng-alex: on it — once infra signals rollback, we'll shift 100% back to primary fleet and validate cert+SNI alignment.
eng-sam: tests to run after rollback:
- `openssl s_client -connect identity.hydra.vpc:443 -servername hydra.tenant-12.vpc.redwood -cert client.pem -key client.key`
- automated smoke: `curl -v --cert client.pem: -k https://identity.hydra.vpc/v1/introspect`
laura_ops: infra reports rollback complete at 09:25:12Z.
deploy-bot: Rollback event: edge-rewrite:v3.4.0 restored to eu-central-1 at 2026-03-15T09:25:12Z.
sre-jordan: shifting traffic back now.
laura_ops: moving 40% -> primary. Monitoring.
laura_ops: primary fleet TLS handshakes healthy; sample logs show expected SNI.
laura_ops: moving remaining 60%.
laura_ops: 100% back to primary fleet. Error rate normalized to baseline ~0.2%.
sec-irene: customer confirms session creation restored for affected users. Thank you.
dan_oncall: brief timeline for postmortem notes:
- root cause: edge TLS hostname rewrite in eu-central replaced tenant SNI with edge hostname, breaking tenant-specific mTLS verification in our identity-proxy.
- mitigation: route to fallback auth-bridge; rollback edge rewrite; validate SNI on post-rollback.
- customer impact: Hydra enterprise (tenant-12) session creation failures in eu-central for ~13 minutes (start 09:12Z, full resolution ~09:25Z), transient token validation errors for some users.
- action items:
  * infra/edge: add integration test to detect SNI preservation during host header/certificate rewrite (owner: infra-edge, ETA: 2w)
  * auth-proxy: add a graceful fallback mode for known enterprise tenants that can be auto-enabled on detection (owner: eng-auth, ETA: 3w)
  * runbook: add a specific playbook for SNI rewrite incidents and customer fallback routing (owner: laura_ops, ETA: 1w)
eng-alex: I'll take auth-proxy action item.
sec-irene: customer requests visibility once runbook is ready. We'll coordinate.
laura_ops: closing alert, will file incident ticket and schedule postmortem sync. Thanks all :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Alert resolved — P1 closed at 2026-03-15T09:36:40Z (duration 24m 28s).
